name: General MIDI Boop
summary: Central Raspberry Pi orchestration system for discovering, adapting, arranging and playing a complete mechanical MIDI orchestra.
description: General MIDI Boop is the control center of the GMB ecosystem rather than a simple MIDI player. It combines instrument discovery and GMB v2 capability descriptors, automatic channel assignment, note-range/polyphony/drum adaptation, multi-transport MIDI connectivity, live routing and virtual controls, latency-aware playback, loop and multitrack arrangement tools, instrument-oriented MIDI editing, optional local audio-to-MIDI transcription, and synchronized lighting/show control. The touch-friendly web interface is designed to run locally on a Raspberry Pi so an orchestra can operate without a cloud backend.

notes: Documented Raspberry Pi targets are 3B+, 4 and 5.
The host is designed as a local/offline-first appliance with a touch-friendly web interface.
The orchestration layer supports an orchestra of up to 16 instruments.

transports.notes: Automatic discovery and hot-plug support are implemented; physical validation depends on host USB/ALSA hardware.
Implemented through the host Bluetooth stack; requires the corresponding Raspberry Pi Bluetooth services.
Network MIDI is implemented but remains explicitly experimental and is not documented as complete AppleMIDI/RFC 6295 compliance.
Physical MIDI over Raspberry Pi GPIO UART at standard MIDI baud rate.

notes: This project is the GMB host/orchestrator; protocol fields describe the instrument-recognition and capability protocol it consumes.
The current codebase includes the v2 handshake, segmented descriptor transfer, capability resolution and descriptor-driven instrument configuration.
Power requirements are those of the selected Raspberry Pi and attached MIDI/lighting interfaces; GMB is software, not an actuator power platform.

documentation.label: GMB v2 SysEx identity and capability protocol

warnings: RTP-MIDI/network MIDI remains experimental and is not presented as complete AppleMIDI/RFC 6295 compatibility.
Hardware-dependent paths such as BLE, GPIO MIDI and Raspberry Pi GPIO lighting require validation on the target host and peripherals.
Lighting uses a multi-driver architecture; protocol/driver maturity depends on the selected backend and target environment.

The General MIDI Boop repository has historically bundled third-party web/audio/icon assets with licensing caveats; GMB HUB does not copy those assets and links only to project-owned interface screenshots.
